Hebrew says “hates hand-strikings,” retaining the gesture of pledging; BSB says “hates indebtedness.”
“Only” before wealth is not expressed in Hebrew; both clauses repeat the verb for holding fast.
Hebrew explicitly contrasts “his soul” and “his flesh”; BSB has “himself” in both clauses.
Hebrew says “wage of falsehood” and “reward of truth”; BSB uses “empty” and “true” and supplies “reaps.”

Hebrew says more “is added,” rather than making the giver the active subject of gaining.
Hebrew says the soul is “made fat” and uses watering imagery; BSB says “prosper” and “refresh.”
Hebrew places blessing on the seller’s “head”; BSB turns this into the verb “crown.”
Hebrew says “seeks favor,” rather than “finds favor.”
